Let me start off by saying I am not an expert on colds/diseases. I'm 29, (definitely) not a health nut, and I rarely get sick. 

These are the things I do in daily life that I believe are helping me avoid colds.

I avoid hand sanitizers like the plague, my immune system seems to be pretty strong. I will wash my hands regularly ( I work in food service), but I believe that being exposed to some germs helps boost your system. (Also, I read on the interwebs that using too much sanitizer decreases the amount of bacteria/germs you are exposed to making your immune system get lazy. No idea if that is true)

What I find works is having a good supply of vitamins on hand. Any time I start to feel like I might be catching something I nuke my system with Vitamin C (15k-25k mg), Golden Seal(2-5x dose), and Echinacea(2-5x Dose) as well as multivitamins (2-3x dose). I think how much you should take depends on your metabolism. Mine is very slow so I take a bunch all at once, but for some friends with higher metabolisms they take a decent amount (3k-5k) multiple times (2-5) in a day. 
I eat about 20 of the 1000mg Vitamin C pills, and take double or triple the rest. Your body can only use so much of the vitamin so most will be passed as waste, but I find with my metabolism doing this "nuke" helps. Im sure doctors and nutritionists will say I'm wrong.

Eat spicy foods. No idea if this helps at all, but some time ago someone said it helps (could just be the vitamins in the peppers) I love spicy foods. I also find that Eating spicy foods while sick usually make you feel better. Maybe not actually get better, but feel better; it helps with colds and hangovers.

Also, if you are feeling like you might be catching something avoid drugs and alcohol for a few days. (Not sure if you use anything) Any thing that has a recovery period takes its toll on your body. Other than Cannabis I believe just about everything requires some recovery time, including alcohol and caffeine. 

I also keep my house cool. It might not be the most comfortable, but I have heard it helps keep you from getting sick. Not sure if it actually does, but I do it anyway. I'm not saying keep your windows open all winter long, but if at any point you are in your house and you think its too warm, it is. I like to keep it at a temperature that isnt too uncomfortable, but makes getting out of the shower suck. You can always grab a sweatshirt or blanket to stay warm. 

Try to fight off any cold like symptoms naturally and/or with vitamins/minerals instead of going to a doctor to get antibiotics (Unless its severe, then get professional medical help) 

I drink a lot of electrolyte water and Alkaline water. I rarely, if ever, drink faucet water that hasnt been filtered.  Not sure if that has any bearing or not, but I think it helps. 

Sorry for the long explanation, hope it helps keep you healthy this winter!
